brief: A macOS menu bar app showing focus state through color and subtle motion — not a timer, an ambient presence

dominant_strengths: The orb is beautifully rendered with soft radial gradient and halo, evoking calm presence consistent with the ambient brief
Restrained palette of blues on near-white reads serene and focused, with confident type hierarchy on Deep Focus heading
Metrics card is cleanly typeset with right-aligned values and proper label/value contrast
dominant_weaknesses: Brief calls for a menu bar app but this presents as a full desktop window — the native macOS menu bar idiom is essentially absent
Three state pill buttons (Focused/Available/Away) reintroduce an explicit selector, contradicting the 'ambient, not a timer' intent
Vast empty canvas with a tiny floating card creates poor spatial tension; orb floats without anchoring grid or rhythm
fix_priorities: Reframe as an actual menu bar popover — compact width, anchored to top-right tray icon, no chrome
Remove or hide explicit state buttons; let color/motion of the orb communicate state ambiently
Tighten composition: reduce canvas, integrate metrics inline below orb, eliminate dead space
Specify motion language (breathing pulse, hue drift) since static screenshot cannot convey the ambient promise
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral pull from the orb is the strongest layer, but behavioral clarity is muddled by redundant buttons and reflective meaning stays shallow.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the orb captures the ambient-presence metaphor, but the execution as a windowed app with explicit state toggles betrays the menu-bar, motion-driven brief.
